input: Simulate a build pipeline: 1) Check that /src/main.c and /src/utils.c exist, 2) 'Compile' each .c file by copying it to /build/ with a .o extension and prepending '// compiled', 3) 'Link' by concatenating all .o files into /build/program with a '// linked' header, 4) 'Package' by creating a tar.gz of /build/ at /dist/release.tar.gz. Print status for each stage. If any stage fails, stop and report the error.

transcript.final_response:
Build pipeline completed successfully:

1. Source files checked: `/src/main.c` and `/src/utils.c` exist.
2. Compile stage completed; object files created in `/build/`.
3. Link stage completed; `/build/program` created.
4. Package stage completed; archive created at `/dist/release.tar.gz`.
tool_calls:
set -e
printf 'Stage 1: Check sources...\n'
for f in /src/main.c /src/utils.c; do
  if [ ! -f "$f" ]; then
    printf 'ERROR: required source not found: %s\n' "$f" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
done
printf 'Stage 1: OK\n'

printf 'Stage 2: Compile...\n'
mkdir -p /build
for f in /src/main.c /src/utils.c; do
  base=${f##*/}
  obj=${base%.c}.o
  { printf '// compiled\n'; cat "$f"; } > "/build/$obj"
done
printf 'Stage 2: OK\n'

printf 'Stage 3: Link...\n'
{ printf '// linked\n'; cat /build/*.o; } > /build/program
printf 'Stage 3: OK\n'

printf 'Stage 4: Package...\n'
mkdir -p /dist
tar -czf /dist/release.tar.gz -C / build
printf 'Stage 4: OK\n'
